newsitem.title: DENMARK: Lauritzen sell shipyard share to Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Lauritzen sell shipyard share to Malaysia.

text.p: Danish shipbuilding and shipping group J.Lauritzen A/S said on Wednesday it sold a 48 percent shareholding in its Danyard A/S shipyard unit for $100 million to Malaysia's Penang Shipbuilding Construction SDN BHD (PSC).
It said that a letter of intent was signed with PSC in Kuala Lumpur at the weekend and that the deal was subject to the approval of the Malaysian authorities.
Lauritzen said that at the same time it was hiving off subsidiary Danyard Aalborg from Danyard A/S as a separate company dealing only in Danish shipping activities.
It said that PSC would take a 40 percent shareholding in Danyard Aalborg along with its 48 percent shareholding in the main Danyard unit.
Danyard has incurred major losses in recent years due to stiff overseas competion, production problems and a weaker dollar.

Announcing group losses of 199 million crowns for the first half of 1996 last August, Lauritzen repeated earlier warnings that it would be forced to end shipbuilding at loss-making Danyard in 1998 unless there was a sharp change in market conditions.
